lines.text: Push a heavy box across carpet, and the floor grips back, up to a point. A tire works the same way, forwards, backwards or sideways.
How hard it grips depends on how hard the tire is pressed down. Press harder, more grip.
So think of grip as a budget, set by the weight on each tire. Forces, grip and weight are always red.
Speeding up, braking and turning all spend it. Spend more than you have, and the tire slips.
Here's the twist: the budget doesn't stay put.
When a bus pulls away, standing riders lean back. Their feet go with the bus, but their bodies lag behind.
A robot does the same. Its weight sits above the floor, so speeding up shifts weight onto the back wheels.
Back tires get pressed harder and get a bigger budget. Front tires get lighter and a smaller one.
The catch: our four modules push about the same amount. So the light front wheels run out of grip first.
